ei.title: A Turning Point in Human History
ei.subject: 올림포스전국연합고1_2026

fullPassage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as "natural" to human beings, appears to have had much to recommend it. Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors enjoyed abundant food, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very few diseases. If this is true, it is not clear why so many humans settled in permanent villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals: cultivating fields was hard work, and it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root. Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture undoubtedly led to a high increase in population density. This period, known as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development, opening the way to the growth of the first towns and cities, and eventually leading to settled "civilizations."

questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as "natural" to human beings, appears to have had much to recommend it. Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors enjoyed (A)[abundant / scarce] food, obtainable without excessive effort, and (B)[suffered / caused] very few diseases. If this is true, it is not clear why so many humans settled in (C)[temporary / permanent] villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals: cultivating fields was hard work, and it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root. Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture undoubtedly led to a high increase in population density. This period, known as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development, opening the way to the growth of the first towns and cities, and eventually leading to settled "civilizations."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) abundant=풍부한, (B) suffered=(병을) 앓았다, (C) permanent=영구적인
det.analysis:
✅ ① abundant — suffered — permanent: 원문 일치. 조상들이 풍부한(abundant) 식량을 누리고 질병을 거의 앓지(suffered) 않았으며, 많은 인간이 영구적인(permanent) 마을에 정착했다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ② scarce — suffered — permanent: (A) scarce(부족한)는 '풍부한(abundant)' 식량이라는 맥락과 반대
❌ ③ abundant — caused — permanent: (B) caused(야기했다)는 질병을 '앓았다(suffered)'는 맥락과 다른 의미
❌ ④ abundant — suffered — temporary: (C) temporary(일시적인)는 '영구적인(permanent)' 마을이라는 맥락과 반대
det.tip: abundant food(풍부한 식량) / suffered very few diseases(질병을 거의 앓지 않음) / permanent villages(영구적인 마을)

questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as "natural" to human beings, appears to have had much to recommend it. Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors enjoyed abundant food, obtainable without (A)[excessive / minimal] effort, and suffered very few diseases. Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture (B)[undoubtedly / doubtfully] led to a high increase in population (C)[scarcity / density]. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) excessive=과도한, (B) undoubtedly=의심의 여지 없이, (C) density=밀도
det.analysis:
❌ ① minimal — undoubtedly — density: (A) minimal(최소한의)은 '과도한(excessive)' 노력 없이라는 맥락에서 원문과 다름
❌ ② excessive — doubtfully — density: (B) doubtfully(의심스럽게)는 '의심의 여지 없이(undoubtedly)'와 반대
✅ ③ excessive — undoubtedly — density: 원문 일치. 과도한(excessive) 노력 없이 식량을 얻었고, 농업이 의심의 여지 없이(undoubtedly) 인구 밀도(density)의 큰 증가를 가져왔다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ④ excessive — undoubtedly — scarcity: (C) scarcity(부족)는 인구 '밀도(density)'의 증가라는 맥락과 다름
det.tip: without excessive effort(과도한 노력 없이) / undoubtedly led to(의심의 여지 없이 이어짐) / population density(인구 밀도)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) recommend=권할 만하다, (B) cultivating=경작하는 것, (C) turning=전환(의)
det.analysis:
❌ ① discourage — cultivating — turning: (A) discourage(단념시키다)는 수렵채집 생활이 '권할 만한(recommend)' 점이 많았다는 맥락과 반대
❌ ② recommend — abandoning — turning: (B) abandoning(버리는 것)은 밭을 '경작하는(cultivating)' 것이라는 맥락과 반대
❌ ③ recommend — cultivating — stopping: (C) stopping(멈춤)은 인류 발전의 '전환점(turning point)'이라는 맥락과 다름
✅ ④ recommend — cultivating — turning: 원문 일치. 수렵채집 생활은 권할 만한(recommend) 점이 많았고, 밭을 경작하는(cultivating) 것은 힘든 일이었으며, 신석기 시대는 큰 전환점(turning point)이었다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
det.tip: much to recommend it(권할 만한 점) / cultivating fields(밭 경작) / a major turning point(큰 전환점)

questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as "natural" to human beings, appears to have had much to recommend it. If this is true, it is not clear why so many humans settled in ②<u>permanent</u> villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals: cultivating fields was hard work, and it was in farming villages that ③<u>epidemic</u> diseases first took root. Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture ④<u>doubtfully</u> led to a high increase in population density. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 농업은 '의심의 여지 없이(undoubtedly)' 인구 증가를 가져왔다. doubtfully(의심스럽게)는 반대 의미
det.analysis:
❌ ① abundant — 원문 일치. 조상들이 풍부한 식량을 누렸다는 맥락에 적절
❌ ② permanent — 원문 일치. 영구적인 마을에 정착했다는 맥락에 적절
❌ ③ epidemic — 원문 일치. 농경 마을에서 전염병이 처음 뿌리내렸다는 맥락에 적절
✅ ④ doubtfully — 원문은 undoubtedly(의심의 여지 없이). 'agriculture doubtfully led to a high increase'는 농업이 인구 증가를 가져왔는지 의심스럽다는 뜻이 되어, 분명히 증가를 가져왔다는 맥락과 모순 ←정답
det.tip: undoubtedly led to a high increase in population density — 의심의 여지 없이 인구 증가를 가져옴

det.korean: 조상들은 '풍부한(abundant)' 식량을 누렸다. scarce(부족한)는 반대 의미

det.tip: permanent(영구적인) ↔ temporary(일시적인). lasting·stable·fixed는 유사어

questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as "natural" to human beings, appears to have had much to recommend it. Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors enjoyed abundant food, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very few diseases. If this is true, it is not clear why so many humans settled in permanent villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals: cultivating fields was hard work, and it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root. Whatever its <u>immediate</u> effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture undoubtedly led to a high increase in population density. This period, known as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development, opening the way to the growth of the first towns and cities, and eventually leading to settled "civilizations."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 immediate와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: immediate=즉각적인 → delayed=지연된
det.analysis:
✅ ① delayed: delayed(지연된)는 immediate(즉각적인)의 반의어 ←정답
❌ ② instant: instant(즉각적인)는 immediate와 유사한 동의어
❌ ③ sudden: sudden(갑작스러운)은 immediate와 유사한 의미
❌ ④ prompt: prompt(신속한)는 immediate와 유사한 의미
det.tip: immediate(즉각적인) ↔ delayed(지연된). instant·sudden·prompt는 유사어

questions.passage:
(A) Despite all the recent changes, one basic fact <u>remains</u> true: people need real connection.
(B) Examination of human <u>remains</u> from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors enjoyed abundant food.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)에서 밑줄 친 remains의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: remains: (A) 한 가지 사실이 여전히 ~이다(동사) / (B) 초기 사회의 인간 유해(명사)
det.analysis:
✅ ① (A) 여전히 ~이다 — (B) 유해/유적: (A)는 한 사실이 여전히 참이다(동사), (B)는 초기 사회의 인간 유해(명사)라는 뜻으로 다의어의 두 의미를 올바르게 연결 ←정답
❌ ② (A) 남다 — (B) 나머지: (B)의 remains는 '나머지'가 아닌 유해
❌ ③ (A) 여전히 ~이다 — (B) 소문: (B)의 remains는 소문이 아닌 유해
❌ ④ (A) 유해 — (B) 여전히 ~이다: (A)는 명사 유해가 아닌 동사, (B)는 동사가 아닌 명사 유해
det.tip: remains: ① (동사) 여전히 ~이다/남다 ② (명사, 복수) 유해/유적 ③ (명사) 나머지

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a person related to you who lived a long time ago"

det.korean: ancestor=조상 (오래전에 살았던, 당신과 혈연으로 이어진 사람)
det.analysis:
❌ ① disease: disease(질병)는 사람이 아닌 병
✅ ② ancestor: ancestor(조상)는 오래전에 살았던 혈연 관계의 사람으로 영영 정의와 정확히 일치 ←정답
❌ ③ village: village(마을)는 사람이 아닌 장소
❌ ④ effort: effort(노력)는 사람이 아닌 행위
det.tip: ancestor = 조상. a person related to you who lived long ago가 핵심

questions.passage: If this is true, it is not clear why so many humans settled in permanent villages and __________ (develop) agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals. Cultivating fields was hard work, and it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: 과거시제 settled와 and로 병렬되는 과거시제 동사 developed
det.analysis: 'so many humans settled in permanent villages and __________ agriculture'에서 과거시제 동사 settled와 and로 병렬되는 자리이므로, 동사원형 develop이 아니라 과거시제 developed가 와야 한다. develop → developed
det.tip: 과거시제 병렬: settled ... and developed (둘 다 과거형)

questions.passage: Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture __________ (undoubted) led to a high increase in population density. This period, known as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: 동사 led를 수식하는 부사 undoubtedly (의심의 여지 없이)
det.analysis: 'agriculture __________ led to a high increase'에서 동사 led를 수식하는 자리이므로, 형용사 undoubted가 아니라 부사 undoubtedly가 와야 한다. undoubted → undoubtedly
det.tip: undoubted(형용사) → undoubtedly(부사). 동사 led를 수식하므로 부사형

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: took root=뿌리내렸다/자리 잡았다 — 농경 마을에서 전염병이 처음 자리 잡았다
det.analysis:
❌ ① died out(사라졌다): 전염병이 '처음' 발생해 자리 잡았다는 맥락과 반대
❌ ② went away(없어졌다): 전염병이 생겨난 맥락과 반대
❌ ③ stayed hidden(숨어 있었다): 전염병이 뚜렷이 자리 잡았다는 맥락과 다름
✅ ④ took root(뿌리내렸다/자리 잡았다): 농경 마을에서 전염병이 처음으로 뿌리내렸다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
det.tip: epidemic diseases first took root — 전염병이 처음 뿌리내렸다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: turning point=전환점 — 신석기 시대는 인류 발전의 큰 전환점이었다
det.analysis:
❌ ① dead end(막다른 길): 도시 성장과 문명으로 이어진 발전의 맥락과 반대
❌ ② minor step(사소한 단계): 'major(큰)'와 모순
✅ ③ turning point(전환점): 신석기 시대가 인류 발전의 큰 전환점으로, 최초의 도시 성장과 정착 문명으로 이어졌다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ④ short break(짧은 휴식): 인류 발전의 중대한 전환이라는 맥락과 다름
det.tip: a major turning point in human development — 인류 발전의 큰 전환점
